decision: adapt (idea); clean-room shape only, source game unnamed so category-level
rule: A monster row (size, race, element with level 1 to 4, class, AI, modes) plus an ordered list of ability rows keyed by monster id. A scan tries rows in order: state gate, shared per-skill cooldown, rate roll (out of 10,000) before the condition, condition check, then range and target gate, where a failure ends the scan by default. A family is a display name shared across size, element and AI variants. Elemental families use four names times three sizes at tier 100 plus five large rows at tier 200; each size carries its own mode skills, and the summon skill picks the size by skill level.

data_fields.name: ability.rate
data_fields.unit: chance per try, 0..1 (donor uses out of 10000)

keep: A family as a shared name across size, element and AI variants
One swapped ability row per variant (elemental modes)
Ordered ability rows with a rate and a cooldown shared per skill id, so a swap does not reset a sibling's timing
Rate roll before condition check (cheap rejection)
State-keyed rows (idle, walk, loot, dead) as data for ambient and death behaviour
Attackers-on-me condition as the many-vs-one gate
change: Rates out of 10000 become 0..1 floats in our data
Range-fail rule: pick one explicit behaviour (stop the scan or skip the row) and test it; donor exposes both as bit 0x1000

D1: rude-attack count is reset when the condition passes, before the cast; if the target or range then fails, the reaction is lost. Fix: reset only after the cast call returns success (mob.cpp 4367-4369, then 4477-4488)
Checked, not a defect: summon level read from variant size (elemental.cpp 56) holds because skill level maps to size (skill.cpp 14652, MaxLevel 3). Fragile: pass skill_lv into elemental_create
look_test: Three of one family side by side at 375 wide: small, medium, large, same silhouette, different tint. Dom checks whether he reads one family at a glance and whether size reads as a step up. Then one same-size sibling with a different ability row (a ring or wedge before the cast): does the wind-up read before the hit, and can he tell the siblings apart without the name. Compare with a flat version of three unrelated shapes.
